title: Identification of Iron-Sulfur (Fe-S) Cluster and Zinc (Zn) Binding Sites Within Proteomes Predicted by DeepMind's AlphaFold2 Program Dramatically Expands the Metalloproteome
summary: A computational screen of AlphaFold2-predicted proteomes identified thousands of candidate iron-sulfur and zinc-binding sites, including recovery of many sites already recorded in UniProt. The work expands a computationally inferred set of metalloprotein candidates; unverified predictions are not experimentally established binding sites.
ai_technology: AlphaFold2 predicted proteome structures were computationally screened for Fe-S and Zn coordination geometries.
organization: University of California San Diego; University of California, San Francisco

source_review.scope: Primary source full text, including Methods and Results; first result-bearing version checked against primary publication metadata.

evidence.tested: Predicted structures from multiple proteomes were screened for metal-coordination geometries and compared with known UniProt annotations.
evidence.unknown: Candidate sites are computational predictions; structural screening and recovery of known annotations do not experimentally verify new metal binding.
